summary: Decision 8 pass for batch rs-whistleblowing-2: rules each document states that were already recorded from other sources are now recorded from that document too.

program_rules.applies_to: covered judicial or administrative action (must exceed)
program_rules.quote: A “covered judicial or administrative action” is “any judicial or administrative action brought by the Commission under [the CEA] that results in monetary sanctions exceeding $1,000,000.” 7 U.S.C. § 26(a)(1).
program_rules.notes: Quotes the statute. Also restated at PDF p. 7 (NCAs posted for orders imposing "more than $1 million in monetary sanctions") and in Note 5 ("monetary sanctions exceeding $1 million").

program_rules.applies_to: sanctions go to the Customer Protection Fund only while its balance is at or below this level
program_rules.location: PDF p. 25, Notes to the financial statements, Note 1.H
program_rules.quote: Per the Act, no sanction collected by the Commission can be deposited into the Fund if the Fund’s balance exceeds $100 million.
program_rules.notes: Also stated in Note 1.G (PDF p. 24): "unless the balance of the Fund at the time the monetary judgment is collected exceeded $100 million".

program_rules.location: p. 3, Section III (Legal Analysis), Rule 165.9 framework
program_rules.quote: Not satisfying any one of the positive factors does not mean that the award percentage must be less than 30%, and the converse is true.
program_rules.notes: The order states the 10-30% range through its description of the Rule 165.9 framework, not as a separate sentence; the same paragraph adds that a significant whistleblower 'could receive 30%'.

program_rules.location: p. 3, Section III (Legal Analysis), Rule 165.9 framework
program_rules.quote: Not having any one of the negative factors does not mean the award percentage must be greater than 10%.
program_rules.notes: The order states the 10-30% range through its description of the Rule 165.9 framework; the same paragraph adds that a whistleblower with limited assistance 'may receive 10%'.

program_rules.applies_to: whether an award must be paid to an eligible whistleblower
program_rules.quote: Section 23(b)(1) of the CEA requires the Commission to pay an award to an individual who voluntarily provides the Commission with original information that leads to the successful enforcement of a covered or related action.

program_rules.location: p. 4, Section III (Legal Analysis), Rule 165.9 framework
program_rules.quote: Not satisfying any one of the positive factors does not mean that the award percentage must be less than 30%, and the converse is true.
program_rules.notes: The order states the 10-30% range through its description of the Rule 165.9 framework, not as a separate sentence; the same paragraph adds that a significant whistleblower 'could receive 30%'.

program_rules.location: p. 4, Section III (Legal Analysis), Rule 165.9 framework
program_rules.quote: Not having any one of the negative factors does not mean the award percentage must be greater than 10%.
program_rules.notes: The order states the 10-30% range through its description of the Rule 165.9 framework; the same paragraph adds that a whistleblower with limited assistance 'may receive 10%'.

program_rules.applies_to: whether an award must be paid to an eligible whistleblower
program_rules.quote: Section 23(b)(1) of the CEA requires the Commission to pay an award to an individual who voluntarily provides the Commission with original information that leads to the successful enforcement of a covered or related action.

program_rules.applies_to: all rewards in a calendar year, unless waived by the President
program_rules.quote: the total amount of rewards paid pursuant to this section may not exceed $25 million in any calendar year.
program_rules.notes: Valid from enactment (1 Jan 2021, printed in the page header); sec. 9703(i) ends the pilot 'three years after the date of the enactment of this Act' (PDF p. 1451), i.e. 1 Jan 2024, as on the row from the HTML copy of the same law.

program_rules.applies_to: per reward, unless the Secretary personally authorizes more and notifies Congress
program_rules.quote: No reward paid under this section may exceed $5 million, unless the Secretary
program_rules.notes: Validity as for the annual cap: enactment 1 Jan 2021 to the three-year sunset in sec. 9703(i).

program_rules.quote: The Secretary of the Treasury may, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Attorney General, and in consultation, as appropriate, with the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies, pay a reward to any individual
program_rules.notes: The Secretary 'may' pay. Validity as for the caps.

program_rules.applies_to: section 7623(b) awards (IRS generally required to pay)
program_rules.quote: For information provided to the IRS after December 19, 2006, new section 7623(b) of the Internal Revenue Code (the Code) generally requires the IRS to pay awards
program_rules.notes: Also in the statute reprinted in Appendix A (PDF p. 13): the individual 'shall ... receive as an award at least 15 percent'.

program_rules.applies_to: section 7623(b)(6)(C): information must be submitted under penalty of perjury
program_rules.quote: No award may be made under this subsection based on information submitted to the Secretary unless such information is submitted under penalty of perjury.

program_rules.applies_to: "proceeds" include criminal fines and civil forfeitures and violations of reporting requirements (7623(c)(2))
program_rules.location: PDF p. 4, Background and Program Evolution
program_rules.quote: On February 9, 2018, Section 41108 of the BBA 2018 amended IRC § 7623 by adding a new subsection (c): Proceeds—For purposes of this section, the term ‘proceeds’ includes—(1) penalties, interest, additions to tax, and additional amounts provided under the internal revenue laws, and (2) any proceeds arising from laws for which the Internal Revenue Service is authorized to administer, enforce, or investigate, including—(A) criminal fines and civil forfeitures, and (B) violations of reporting requirements.

program_rules.applies_to: section 7623(a) awards (submissions that do not meet the 7623(b) criteria)
program_rules.location: PDF p. 4, Background and Program Evolution
program_rules.quote: If a submission does not meet the criteria for IRC § 7623(b) consideration, the Whistleblower Office may consider it for an award pursuant to its discretionary authority under IRC § 7623(a).
program_rules.notes: No existing row has this exact scope; closest are the TIGTA 2023 and eCFR rows on 7623(a) discretion.

program_rules.applies_to: section 7623(b) awards when the Secretary proceeds with an action based on the information
program_rules.quote: IRC § 7623 provides for awards, in some cases mandatory, when the IRS proceeds with an action based on a whistleblower’s information.
program_rules.notes: The report says 'in some cases mandatory' (the 7623(b) programme; PDF p. 4: 'the IRS will pay an award of at least 15 percent').

program_rules.applies_to: section 7623(b)(6)(C): information must be submitted under penalty of perjury
program_rules.quote: No award may be made under this subsection based on information submitted to the Secretary unless such information is submitted under penalty of perjury.
program_rules.notes: Statute reprinted in the report. The narrative (printed p. 3, PDF p. 5) also says Notice 2008-4 'includes the requirement that the information be submitted by an individual, under penalty of perjury'.

program_rules.applies_to: section 7623(a) awards (submissions that do not meet the 7623(b) criteria)
program_rules.quote: If the submission does not meet the criteria for 7623(b) consideration, it may be considered for an award under the pre-Act discretionary authority (what is now section 7623(a)).

ledger.contains: CFTC report to Congress for FY2017 (28 pp.; pp. 6-7 are scanned images with an OCR text layer): no awards paid, 2 Final Orders denying 2 applications; 2017 rule amendments (proposed Aug 2016, effective 31 Jul 2017; events and the 90-day filing rule); Preliminary Determinations over $45 million after the rules took effect; award history (four awards, ~$11 million; already recorded); 465 TCRs with Figure 1 FY2012-2017 and 110 non-whistleblower tips (61 e-mails/other + 49 SEC referrals); 30 NCAs; 74 award claims with Figure 2 FY2012-2017; outreach (30,000 e-mail subscribers, 111,000 page views: no indicator, not recorded); confidentiality reviews of document requests (new indicator); customer education (out of scope); fund table incl. $45.5 million contingent award claims (checks exactly); OIG memo (balance matches); auditors' report; financial statements. Figure values were read by OCR from the chart images (text layer lacks them). Percent increases (70%, 25%) are the source's own calculations and are not recorded. Not extracted, judged out of scope as fund accounting detail: Fund Balance with Treasury, investments, prepayments, payables, leave, software, overhead allocation ($918,000), budgetary resources, cash flow, comparatives. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

CFTC Order Determining Whistleblower Award Claims 24-WB-02 (public version, 4 pp., 4 Jan 2024): award of 20% of sanctions collected to Claimant 1, whose complaint opened the investigation but who gave limited further help (already recorded); denial of Claimant 2. Sanctions ordered, amounts collected, payment amounts, dates and the defendant are redacted; the order does not say whether either claimant was an insider. General text on how award percentages are set (10-30% framework, Rule 165.9) restates rules already in the data. Added: the Claimant 2 denial as its own case row. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

CFTC Order Determining Whistleblower Award Claims 24-WB-03 (public version, 5 pp., 4 Jan 2024): award to Claimant 1 (a fraud victim who complained through an attorney) on a CFTC covered action and a related action, $4,247.22 paid so far on the covered action and zero so far on the related action (already recorded); denial of Claimant 2. Percentages, sanctions ordered and collected, the related-action fine, dates and defendants are redacted. General text on award percentages restates rules already in the data. Added: the Claimant 2 denial as its own case row. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

CFTC press release 6933-14 (20 May 2014): first CFTC whistleblower award, "approximately $240,000" (case already recorded, c-fa652e5107); quotes from officials (more high-quality tips, no figures); programme basics: awards for actions with more than $1 million in sanctions, 10-30% of monies collected, related actions, anti-retaliation. Added the threshold and percentage rules as restated here. "First award" is a word, not recorded as a count. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

CFTC press release 7254-15 (29 Sep 2015): second award, "approximately $290,000" (case already recorded, c-97862e04cf); back-reference to the first award of $240,000 on 20 May 2014 (already recorded from its own order and release, not added again); programme basics (threshold over $1 million, 10-30%, awards paid from the Customer Protection Fund financed by sanctions); official quotes (tips growing, no figures). Added threshold and percentage rules as restated. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

CFTC press release 7351-16 (4 Apr 2016): award of "more than $10 million" (order 16-WB-06; case already recorded, c-b18441e896), largest to date and the third award; confidentiality, programme rules (threshold $1,000,000, related actions, 10-30%, Customer Protection Fund, anti-retaliation); back-reference to the Sept 2015 award of about $290,000 (not added again). Added threshold and percentage rules as restated. Ordinal "third award" not turned into a count. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

CFTC press release 7411-16 (26 Jul 2016): fourth award, "approximately $50,000" (order 16-WB-08; case already recorded, c-20facbf469), third award in 10 months; the award "represents between 10 percent and 30 percent of the monetary sanctions collected to date" (a range, not a stated percentage, so award_pct left empty); programme rules; back-reference to the April 2016 award of more than $10 million (not added again). Added threshold and percentage rules as restated. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

NDAA for FY2021 (Pub. L. 116-283, 1,482 pp.). In scope: sec. 6314 (AML Act of 2020, rewrites 31 U.S.C. 5323: $1,000,000 threshold, awards up to 30% subject to appropriations, discretion, exclusions, anonymous claims through counsel, 30-day appeal, anti-retaliation via Labor Department/district court with 6/3/10-year limits and 2x back pay, confidentiality; repeals 5328; PDF pp. 1211-1217) and sec. 9701-9703 (Kleptocracy Asset Recovery Rewards pilot: $450,000 authorised for FY2021, $25 million annual cap, $5 million per-reward cap, perjury attestation, exclusions, reports, 3-year sunset; PDF pp. 1447-1452). The kleptocracy cap rules and enactment event were already taken from the HTML copy of the same law (usa-pl-116-283-ndaa-fy2021, a different file); not duplicated here, only the perjury rule and the FY2021 authorisation added. Sec. 1238 (State Department rewards for information on foreign election interference) is an informant-reward programme outside the dataset; not recorded. Rest out of scope. Added 7 rules and 1 observation (new indicator). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

DOJ press release 26-71 (29 Jan 2026): first Antitrust Division/USPS whistleblower reward, $1 million, for information leading to EBLOCK Corporation's deferred prosecution agreement and $3.28 million criminal fine (bid rigging and shill bidding on used-vehicle auctions, Nov 2020 - Feb 2022; "$16 million scheme" per a DOJ official); paid six months after the programme started; programme rules (at least $1 million; 15-30%). Case and event already recorded; added the threshold and percentage rules as restated here. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Pilot Program guidance as revised 30 July 2026 (15 pp.): same structure and award scale as the 2024 guidance, with these changes: section now named MLNFS; eligibility for another programme no longer bars an award, only duplicate awards (footnote 3, new factor III.3.b.v on other programmes); eight subject areas (adds federal health care offenses generally, federal contracting fraud, trade/tariff/customs fraud, immigration, sanctions/terrorism/cartels); submissions through the online intake portal. Already in the data: two events (launch, revision). Added eight rules restating the award terms (threshold, 30%/5% scale, 30% presumption on first $10 million, discretion, anonymous via attorney, 120-day internal window, 90-day claim window). Not recorded as rules (no fitting type): no award above $500 million net proceeds (in notes), $500,000 congressional-notification trigger (p. 14), three-submission bar, 7-day attorney deadline. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IRS Whistleblower Program FY2014 report to Congress (24 pp.): executive summary (record 14,365 claims; 101 awards totalling $52,281,628 before a $3,764,722 sequestration cut, 16.9 percent of collections); program history and rules; final regulations 12 Aug 2014 and Deputy Commissioner memo 20 Aug 2014 (events already recorded); eleven 7623(b) payments since FY2011; staffing (40 to 43, out of scope); legislative proposals; Appendix A statute; Table 1 claims received and open by year of receipt (pre-2010 to 2014, as of 14 May 2015); Table 2 FY2014 receipts by operating division and claim type; Table 3 FY2014 closures by reason and year of receipt (80 percent received in FY2013-14); Table 4 open potential-7623(b) claims by 21 statuses; Table 5 days in status; Table 6 awards FY2010-2014 incl. collections over $2 million and percentages. Added: Table 1 total, Table 2 by division, Table 3 by year of receipt, Tables 4-5 in full, Table 6 over-$2-million and percentage rows, the 80 percent statement, restated rules. All tables add up. The rise of 3,845 claims on FY2013 is a difference and is not recorded. Note: Table 6 award amounts are before sequestration (the FY2014 rows already in the data carry no before_sequestration flag). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IRS Whistleblower Program FY2019 report to Congress (19 pp., Rev. 2-2020; Figure 2 revised 3 Feb 2020): Director's message (181 awards, $120,305,278; proceeds $616,773,127 split Title 26 / non-Title 26; 282 foreign whistleblowers; percentage changes not recorded); background, rules, BBA 2018 and Taxpayer First Act 2019 (event already recorded); GAO follow-up; staffing (37 FTE, Figure 1, out of scope); issues of interest; Table 1 FY2017-2019; Figure 2 claims paid and days/years by type; Figure 3 FY2019 claim numbers by month and type; Table 2(A) receipts by operating division; Table 2(B) receipts sent to field examination; Figure 4(A) issued/open/closed; Figure 4(B) whistleblowers by region (chart image, OCR); Figure 5 open 7623(b) claims by year of receipt; Table 3 open claims by phase; Table 4 closures by reason with percent and average days. Added the missing rows of Tables 1-4 and Figures 2, 3, 4(B) and 5 (Figure 3 series by stacking order; Figure 5 adds to the Table 3 7623(b) total of 12,174; Figure 4(B) values from OCR), restated rules. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IRS Whistleblower Program first report to Congress (11 pp., 24 Jun 2008), covering the Whistleblower Office's first 12 months: prior law and policy (1/10/15 percent, generally not over $10 million), the 2006 law (15-30 percent, 10 percent for public-source cases, $2 million and $200,000 thresholds, 30-day Tax Court appeal), first Director appointed 2 Feb 2007, staffing (eight, out of scope), intake design, Notice 2008-4 and Form 211 (undated here), interim case management, Ogden consolidation, 116 potential 7623(b) submissions to 31 Jan 2008 (24 alleging over $10 million, 29 more without an amount), FY2007 paid claims over $2 million (12) and over $10 million (3), FY2008 priorities, table of cases received, awards paid, award amounts and collections FY2003-2007 with 35 partial payments ($3.2 million), and an appendix reprinting section 7623. Rules, events and the table were already recorded; added the 24/29 submission splits, the over-$10-million count and one event. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

One-page IRS notice: award payments under section 7623 made in FY2025 are reduced by the FY2025 sequestration rate of 5.7%, whatever the Form 211 date (Budget Control Act 2011 as amended). The rate is already recorded as a rule; nothing else in scope. The file is named fy-2026-sequester-notice.pdf but states the FY2025 rate. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).
